items.stem: In the simplest two-sector circular flow, what do households supply to firms?
items.answer: Factors of production
items.markingKey: Households → factors; firms → goods/services; income flows back.

items.stem: Explain the circular flow of income in a two-sector economy.
items.answer: Households supply factors of production to firms and receive factor incomes; they spend this income on goods and services produced by firms, so money flows round from firms to households and back.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: real flows; 1 mark: money flows; 1 mark: circularity [3]

items.stem: Explain how adding a government sector changes the circular flow.
items.answer: Taxes are withdrawn from the flow and government spending is injected into it; national income depends on the balance between them as well as saving/investment.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: taxes leak; 1 mark: spending injects [2]

items.stem: Consumers in Fendaria buy cars made abroad. Is this an injection into or a leakage from the circular flow?
options: Neither: a transfer within the flow
items.answer: Leakage (withdrawal)
items.markingKey: Leakage (withdrawal): imports send spending out of the domestic flow.

items.stem: Consumers in Loristan buy cars made abroad. Is this an injection into or a leakage from the circular flow? Explain your answer.
items.answer: Leakage (withdrawal): imports send spending out of the domestic flow.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: Leakage (withdrawal); 1 mark: explanation – imports send spending out of the domestic flow. [2]

items.stem: Extract: Exports from Zentara fell from $180 billion to $150 billion as its main trading partner entered a recession. Households, worried about jobs, increased saving. The government responded by raising its spending by $40 billion, funded by borrowing, and kept tax rates unchanged. (a) Identify the injections and leakages mentioned in the extract. (b) Explain whether the extra government spending is enough to offset the fall in exports.
items.answer: (a) Injections: exports, government spending; leakage: saving. (b) Exports fell by $30bn vs extra G $40bn: enough to offset exports; and saving also rose.
items.markingKey: (a) Credit: Injections: exports, government spending; leakage: saving. [2] (b) Credit: Exports fell by $30bn vs extra G $40bn: enough to offset exports; and saving also rose. [2]

items.stem: What is a closed economy?
options: An economy where all firms are state-owned
An economy with no international trade
items.answer: An economy with no international trade
items.markingKey: No exports or imports.

items.stem: Calvania opens up to international trade. Explain how this changes its circular flow of income.
items.answer: Exports become an injection (foreign spending on domestic output) and imports a leakage (domestic spending on foreign output).
items.markingKey: 1 mark: exports injection; 1 mark: imports leakage [2]

items.stem: Leila makes the following statement: ‘In the circular flow, households supply goods and services to firms.’ Identify what is wrong with this reasoning and give the correct explanation.
items.answer: Households supply factors of production; firms supply goods and services to households.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: identifies the error; 1 mark: correct explanation – Households supply factors of production; firms supply goods and services to households. [2]

items.stem: Workers in Westaria pay income tax. Is this an injection into or a leakage from the circular flow?
options: Neither: a transfer within the flow
items.answer: Leakage (withdrawal)
items.markingKey: Leakage (withdrawal): taxation removes income from the flow.

items.answer: (i) Injection (ii) Injection (iii) Injection

items.stem: Which are the three injections into the circular flow?
items.answer: Investment, government spending and exports
items.markingKey: I + G + X.

items.stem: Explain the difference between an injection and a leakage.
items.answer: An injection is spending that enters the circular flow from outside household consumption (I, G, X); a leakage is income that is not passed on as spending on domestic output (S, T, M).
items.markingKey: 1 mark each [2]

items.stem: Explain why imports are a leakage from the circular flow.
items.answer: Spending on imports goes to foreign producers, so it does not become income for domestic factors of production.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: spending leaves country; 1 mark: not domestic income [2]

items.stem: Households in Jovania put part of their income into savings accounts. Is this an injection into or a leakage from the circular flow?
options: Neither: a transfer within the flow
items.answer: Leakage (withdrawal)
items.markingKey: Leakage (withdrawal): saving is income not passed on as spending.

items.stem: The government of Zentara pays nurses’ salaries. Is this an injection into or a leakage from the circular flow? Explain your answer.
items.answer: Injection: government spending adds to the flow.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: Injection; 1 mark: explanation – government spending adds to the flow. [2]

items.stem: Explain why an increase in investment can lead to a larger increase in national income.
items.answer: Investment spending becomes income for workers and firms, who spend part of it, creating further income in successive rounds until leakages rise to match the new injection.

items.stem: Explain how a recession in a major trading partner affects national income.
items.answer: Demand for exports falls, reducing injections; incomes and spending fall in the domestic economy.
